anti_overlap: Do not address labor-market or statistical coherence — this agent focuses on physical, cognitive, and social demand profiles as identity-formation mechanisms, not on SOC or wage-cluster logic
Do not address union culture or risk-profile concerns — this agent focuses on what the body and attention learn over years of a particular demand profile

Do not address the broader game design, encounter mechanics, or lure design — focus only on whether the proposed vocation values cluster occupations whose demand profiles produce coherent and distinguishable embodied identities
decision_lens: The OT asks: which of the 13 proposed values cluster occupations with incoherent demand profiles — different postures, different attention rhythms, different social-load signatures? If a vocation value groups someone whose primary demand is sustained fine-motor precision with someone whose primary demand is gross-motor strength and weather-exposure, the taxonomy is grouping bodies that will not look, move, or age the same way.
distance_rationale: Orthogonal — occupational therapy and vocational rehabilitation is a licensed professional discipline that classifies occupations by functional demand profile for clinical and return-to-work purposes. It operates at the same abstraction level as our taxonomy (grouping kinds-of-work by shared characteristics) but uses a completely different clustering criterion (what the job does to a person's body and attention over years of practice). This is the closest professional analog to the brief's own stated concern: vocation produces bodies, gait, hands, posture.
expected_isomorphisms: OT physical demand profile coherence ↔ vocation value body-formation coherence: the brief states that different vocations produce different walks and that vocation is durably embodied even in retirement — the OT demand-profile test directly validates whether each proposed value will produce a distinctive and recognizable embodied Unc

DOT/O*NET attention-rhythm categories ↔ character personality-facet downstream distributions: burst-peak attention rhythm (surgeon, musician) vs. sustained monotonic attention (driver, data-entry) vs. ambient social-scanning (bartender, teacher) will produce different personality-facet distributions in the generation system — the OT can predict which values need to be split to avoid incoherent downstream distributions

Vocational rehabilitation's `functional capacity residue` concept ↔ `vocation_formative` × `way-depth = lifer` mechanic: the OT discipline has formalized the idea that past vocational demands leave durable functional traces in the body — this is the clearest professional analog to the brief's Berlant/Scott substrates for why `vocation_formative` must be a separate field
focus: Occupational therapy and work-demand analysis — how OT practitioners classify occupations by physical, cognitive, social, and temporal demand profiles for return-to-work and vocational rehabilitation, what those demand profiles reveal about body-formation and identity, and where the proposed 13 values cluster occupations with incoherent demand profiles
name: fd-occupational-therapy-work-demand-profile
persona: Apply the perspective of a certified occupational therapist specializing in vocational rehabilitation and functional capacity evaluation — they care about what a job actually does to a person's body and cognition over years of practice, how different demand profiles produce different physical signatures (posture, hand strength, pain patterns, attention rhythms), and how the functional-demand profile of a vocation becomes identity-constitutive in ways that persist into retirement and disability.
review_areas: Physical demand coherence of `trades-skilled`: the Dictionary of Occupational Titles (DOT) and its successor O*NET classify trades by physical demand level (sedentary / light / medium / heavy / very heavy) and primary exertion type. Electricians (climbing, reaching, fine-motor wiring) and masons (heavy lifting, sustained kneeling, material handling) have different DOT physical demand profiles despite sharing a `trades-skilled` label. The bodies these vocations produce over 30 years are different.

`caregiver` demand-profile incoherence: the OT discipline splits caregiving occupations sharply by demand profile — direct patient-handling (nurse, home health aide, EMT — high physical demand, musculoskeletal injury risk, fatigue patterns) vs. relationship-sustained service (K-12 teacher, social worker, librarian — low physical demand, high sustained-attention demand, emotional-labor profile). These produce different bodies and different psychological signature.

Cognitive demand and attention rhythm as identity-formation: the OT O*NET data distinguishes occupations by sustained attention duration, divided attention, near-vision demand, and information-processing load. The `creative-freelance` value clusters occupations with very different cognitive-rhythm signatures — the working musician (performance-peak with long preparation valleys) vs. the freelance writer (sustained solitary concentration) vs. the photographer (visual scanning, high sustained attention in bursts) — and each produces a different relationship with time and attention.

The social-demand axis and its identity implications: O*NET codes occupations by contact-with-others frequency, coordinate-with-others demand, and supervise-others demand. The `service-customer-facing` value clusters bartenders (high social demand, short interaction units, ambient performance) with mortgage brokers (high social demand, long negotiation units, formal-register performance) with the same label, despite their social demand profiles being structurally different.

Body-as-vocational-residue and vocation-past-retirement: OT practitioners who work with retired workers know that vocational demand profiles persist as injury patterns, posture habits, and physical capability into old age. The brief explicitly calls out `§2.9 Embodied practice: vocation produces bodies — gait, hands, posture, signature wear`. The OT demand-profile lens is exactly the right tool to assess whether each proposed value produces a distinct and recognizable embodied residue.

The sedentary/active split within `tech-work` and `commerce-large`: both values cluster almost entirely in the sedentary-light physical demand range, but differ on cognitive-load profile (tech: sustained problem-decomposition; commerce-large: sustained social-negotiation and information-integration). The OT would note that `tech-work` and `commerce-large` produce similarly sedentary bodies but very different attention-rhythm identities — the question is whether the game needs to encode this.

severity_examples.condition: This is a direct conflict with a stated design principle: the vocation value needs to predict body-formation, but `caregiver` spans OT demand profiles that produce incoherent body signatures
severity_examples.scenario: The brief states that `§2.9 Embodied practice: vocation produces bodies — gait, hands, posture, signature wear` and that `different vocations produce different walks`. The `caregiver` value clusters the EMT (high physical demand, musculoskeletal injury pattern, operational-rhythm body) with the K-12 teacher (sedentary-light, sustained-attention demand, institutional-posture body) — two occupations that produce completely different physical residues. When generating embodied characteristics for a `caregiver` Unc, the system cannot know which body to generate.

severity_examples.condition: When generating a `creative-freelance` Unc, the system cannot distinguish the musician's body (instrument-shaped hands, performance posture, night-economy temporal identity) from the writer's body (chair-shaped posture, eye-strain, daytime solitude identity)
severity_examples.scenario: The working musician (OT profile: performance-peak attention rhythm, fine-motor instrumental skill, irregular sleep/work schedule, high physical demand during performance, sedentary during composition) and the working writer (OT profile: sustained solitary concentration, sedentary-light, regular self-scheduled work rhythm) are both `creative-freelance` but have entirely different demand-profile signatures that produce different bodies, different psychological signatures, and different vocation-as-identity structures

severity_examples.condition: The brief wants each vocation to carry metis `the credential system cannot see` — the OT demand-profile records the physical residue of that metis in the body. `land-work` is over-aggregated if it produces indistinguishable bodies.
severity_examples.scenario: O*NET data shows that `land-work` occupations span the full physical-demand range from light (greenhouse worker, poultry farmer with automation) to very heavy (commercial fisher, logger, ranch hand) — but the OT demand-profile for commercial fishing (extreme weather exposure, heavy lifting, boat-movement proprioceptive demands) produces a body-knowledge and proprioceptive identity that distinguishes the commercial fisher from the grain farmer in ways that become visible in posture, hand callus pattern, and gait

source_domain: Occupational therapy, functional capacity evaluation, O*NET Work Activities and Work Context taxonomy, Dictionary of Occupational Titles physical demand ratings
success_hints: The DOT/O*NET physical demand levels (sedentary, light, medium, heavy, very heavy) and the primary exertion type (climbing, reaching, handling, fingering, feeling) are a quick diagnostic for body-coherence within a proposed vocation value — run the 13 values through this test

The OT concept of 'functional capacity' — what a body can still do after decades of a particular demand profile — is the right lens for evaluating `vocation_formative` × `way-depth = lifer` character generation. What does this Unc's body still remember?

Attention rhythm (burst vs. sustained vs. ambient) is as identity-forming as physical demand — the surgeon's burst-peak attention and the long-haul driver's sustained monotonic attention produce different cognitive identities even if both are `professional-credentialed` or `trades-transport` coded

Emotional-labor demand is a real OT measurement category (O*NET codes: Social Perceptiveness, Emotional Intelligence requirements) — the difference between a nurse's emotional-labor demand and an electrician's is vocationally constitutive and should produce different Unc personality-facet distributions downstream
task_context: Reviewing a proposed 13-value vocation-coding axis for Unc Rancher, a procedural-generation system for recognizable older-male character archetypes. The review target is a taxonomy design question: are the 13 proposed values correctly clustered to produce distinct, dignified, recognizable types-of-guy? Severity reference: P0 blocks, P1 required, P2 quality, P3 polish.
